tasks.short: Explain the eye condition and procedure, show how to use eye drops, select and print leaflets, and record the education given.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist educates patients on ophthalmic procedures and conditions of the eye
Ophthalmic technologist shows appropriate use of medications such as eye drops
Ophthalmic technologist selects and prints patient leaflets
Ophthalmic technologist records the education given as free text

tasks.design: Leaflets are linked to diagnosis and procedure codes in the record ({OTHER}), which lists the right set for the patient to print, so the technologist does not search folders. The education given is recorded with a tick list (condition, procedure, drops technique, leaflets). Explaining and showing drop use stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were searched in folders and education noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Records can link leaflets to diagnosis codes.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who speak other languages need leaflets that do not exist.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a shaky patient to hit their eye with a drop.

reach.learn: Whether they leave with the right leaflets.

evidence.claim: Records can link patient leaflets to diagnosis and procedure codes.
Providers must inform patients and record it in the dossier.

assumptions: Boundary: from the diagnosis made to education recorded; treatment is outside.
Input contract: leaflets linked to codes; fallback is folders.
research_questions: Do patients get the right leaflets more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few leaflets needed; high: many new diagnoses per day.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct staff at the chair, supervise daily work, keep training records, and make the staff rota.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist instructs ophthalmic staff at the chair
Ophthalmic technologist supervises ophthalmic staff's daily work
Ophthalmic technologist keeps staff training records on paper
Ophthalmic technologist makes the staff rota in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Skills signed off for each staff member are recorded on a skills checklist in the learning system ({LMS}). The rota is made in the rostering tool ({HCM}), which checks that each clinic has staff with the needed skills, instead of a spreadsheet. Instructing and supervising staff stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training was kept on paper and rotas built in a spreadsheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems keep skills checklists; rostering tools check skills.
tasks.still_hard: Sick leave changes the rota at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which new colleague needs more time on the slit lamp.

evidence.claim: Learning systems keep skills checklists and rostering tools check skills per shift.
Systems that record staff skills and shifts may need works council consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the staff need to the rota made; hiring is outside.
Input contract: staff skills entered; fallback is paper and spreadsheet.
Instruction and supervision do not change.
research_questions: Do clinics run short of skilled staff less often?

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technologist enters existing skills sign-offs.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small teams; high: large clinics with many rotas.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find patients due for a post-operative call, call them about recovery, record the outcome, and arrange an earlier visit if needed.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist finds patients due for a post-operative call from the surgery list
Ophthalmic technologist calls patients to inquire about their post-operative status
Ophthalmic technologist records the recovery call in free text
Ophthalmic technologist arranges an earlier visit if recovery is not going well

tasks.design: A daily call list in the record ({OTHER}) shows patients one day after surgery with their operation and phone number, so the technologist does not build it from the surgery list. The call is recorded on a short form with the standard recovery questions (pain, vision, redness, drops use) and an outcome. Calling patients and deciding on an earlier visit stay with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Call lists were made by hand and calls recorded in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Records produce call lists from surgery dates and hold structured forms.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who do not answer need several tries.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing worry in a patient's voice that the questions miss.

evidence.claim: Records can produce call lists from surgery dates and hold structured call forms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the surgery list to the visit arranged; treatment is outside.
Input contract: surgery dates in the record; fallback is the paper list.

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technologist adds notes for unusual answers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few operations; high: busy cataract lists.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Show patients how to insert, remove and clean contact lenses, hand out the care leaflet and wearing schedule, and record the instruction.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technologist instructs patients in the care and use of contact lenses
Ophthalmic technologist writes the wearing schedule on the care leaflet by hand
Ophthalmic technologist records the lens instruction as free text

tasks.design: The care leaflet with the patient's wearing schedule is printed from the lens fitting record ({OTHER}), so it is not written by hand. The instruction is recorded with a checklist (insertion, removal, cleaning, schedule, patient manages alone). Showing the patient stays with the technologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Schedules were written by hand and instruction noted in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Records print leaflets from fitting data and hold checklists.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who struggle need notes the checklist does not cover.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a patient who flinches at touching their eye.

reach.learn: Whether instruction is clear in the record.

evidence.claim: Records can print leaflets from fitting data and hold instruction checklists.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lens fitted to instruction recorded; lens fitting is outside.
Input contract: fitting data in the record; fallback is writing by hand.
research_questions: Do lens-care problems at follow-up fall?

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technologist adds notes for patients who struggle.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients who struggle; high: routine instruction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The ophthalmic technologist keeps educating patients, instructing staff and calling patients after surgery; folder searches, paper training records, hand-built lists and free-text notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with more time with patients.
